newsitem.title: RUSSIA: More Russian gems to leak if no De Beers deal-Tass.
newsitem.headline: More Russian gems to leak if no De Beers deal-Tass.

text.p: The head of Russia's diamond producer Almazy-Rossii Sakha said on Friday that the lack of a trade deal between Russia and De Beers would spur illegal trade in Russian gems, Itar-Tass news agency said.

ARS president Vyacheslav Shtyrov also said a draft trade agreement reached in August and presented to the government in October suited both companies, but said that government approval of the deal had been held up while a presidential decree was prepared.
Tass quoted Shtyrov as saying that the legal team of President Boris Yeltsin's administration may have held up the deal.
He said the team may consider the signing of a trade agreement an issue for the president, and not for the government, which is headed by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
Tass gave no details on the nature of the presidential decree.

"We (ARS and De Beers) have conducted intense negotiations for half a year," Shtyrov said. "Today both sides are satisfied by those agreements contained in the trade agreement. But the question is not being brought to a close, and some people are even asserting that the agreement will not be concluded at all."
The mostly-state owned ARS is De Beers' negotiating partner.
Shtyrov's comments raise questions over who in Russia has the right to sign a trade deal -- Yeltsin or Chernomyrdin. The two companies have said in the past that Chernomyrdin has the final word.

De Beers said on Wednesday it had formally notified the government at the highest levels that unless a diamond trade agreement were approved by the end of 1996, it would terminate its interim deal on that date.
It said that if substantial sales of Russian gems outside the interim deal had not taken place this year, it probably would have continued with the temporary export arrangement.
The South African diamond group said its patience had worn thin because Moscow had provided no official word on the status of the agreement since its October submission.
The draft agreement was based on a February memorandum which replaced a five-year agreement that expired in December 1995.
